hypotheses.justification: Lean adds this instance automatically because its type only mentions X, which is already an argument through b. It is never used: the proof applies b ∘ b to both sides of h and simplifies with hb, which uses neither finiteness nor decidability. Injectivity follows from b having the left inverse b ∘ b, so it holds for any type, and vacuously when X is empty. `omit [Fintype X] in` would leave the statement and proof unchanged. It can be deleted together with [DecidableEq X].

Lean adds this instance automatically because its type only mentions X. Neither the statement Function.Injective b nor the proof (congrArg with b ∘ b, then simpa [hb]) needs decidable equality. Injectivity follows from b ∘ b ∘ b = id for any type. `omit [DecidableEq X] in` would leave the proof unchanged. It can be deleted together with [Fintype X].
